DIMS.name: Enterprise Profile
DIMS.summary: A regulated regional bank with fragmented core, digital, risk, and data estate requiring evidence before AI activation.

DIMS.name: Business Functions
DIMS.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

DIMS.name: Org Ownership
DIMS.summary: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.

DIMS.name: Workforce Roles
DIMS.summary: Fraud analyst, AML investigator, loan officer, and contact center roles are target beneficiaries; readiness is not evidenced.

DIMS.name: Applications & Systems
DIMS.summary: Core banking, digital, fraud, AML, loan, CRM, and risk platforms operate with incomplete integration and lineage evidence.

DIMS.name: Data Assets & Integrations
DIMS.summary: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.

DIMS.name: Infrastructure & Platforms
DIMS.summary: Cloud lakehouse and customer 360 foundation are aspirational; current infrastructure evidence is not yet validated.

DIMS.name: Vendors & Contracts
DIMS.summary: CoreBank, FraudShield, ComplyCase, and others carry unlinked SLA obligations, invoice variances, and exit-right gaps.

DIMS.name: IT Budget, Spend & Value
DIMS.summary: FS Demo operates across lending, cards, payments, fraud, AML/KYC, and wealth under strong regulatory oversight.

DIMS.name: Programs & Initiatives
DIMS.summary: Fraud copilot, AML assist, banker assist, regulatory reporting, customer 360, loan automation, and vendor optimization are active hypotheses.

DIMS.name: AI & Automation Use Cases
DIMS.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

DIMS.name: Risks & Controls
DIMS.summary: Regulatory reporting controls, AML reviewer controls, and fair-lending controls lack linkage to certified data products.

DIMS.name: Relationships
DIMS.summary: CIO, CTO, CDAO, and CRO signals indicate decision latency, contract friction, and sequencing risk across initiatives.

DIMS.name: Evidence Sources
DIMS.summary: No finance-approved baselines, realized savings, or ROI evidence exists for any current AI or modernization initiative.

DIMS.name: Metrics & Outcomes
DIMS.summary: False-positive rates, AML case cycle times, handle times, and defect baselines are absent or not finance-approved.

DIMS.name: Industry Context Patterns
DIMS.summary: Regulated banking AI adoption patterns consistently require lineage, model-risk, and explainability before production deployment.

DIMS.name: Expert Lenses
DIMS.summary: Model risk, AML compliance, fair lending, and data governance expert lenses each surface distinct but compounding blockers.

DIMS.name: Managed Services Scope
DIMS.summary: RegOps Managed Services is identified as a vendor; scope, SLA linkage, and accountability boundaries are not confirmed.

DIMS.name: Operational Process Evidence
DIMS.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

profile.meaning: A regulated regional bank with fragmented core, digital, risk, and data estate requiring evidence before AI activation.
profile.observed: Seven strategic AI use cases identified; all gated by lineage, auditability, and model-risk evidence needs.
profile.matters: Control expectations and vendor dependency create compounding risk if AI moves ahead of governance readiness.
profile.supports: No use case is production-ready; all require evidence validation before value claims or deployment decisions.

functions.meaning: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.
functions.observed: Seven use cases span risk, customer experience, operations, and data functions; integration gaps are pervasive.
functions.matters: Siloed functions prevent unified customer view, complicate AI deployment, and fragment control accountability.
functions.supports: Function-level evidence must precede cross-domain AI initiatives; sequencing risk is high without integration proof.

org.meaning: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.
org.observed: Approved answer content, data-quality exceptions, and model-risk approvals lack named owners in current context.
org.matters: Unowned data products and ungoverned AI outputs create audit exposure and slow regulatory response.
org.supports: Ownership assignment is a prerequisite; no AI use case should advance without accountable domain owners confirmed.

workforce.meaning: Fraud analyst, AML investigator, loan officer, and contact center roles are target beneficiaries; readiness is not evidenced.
workforce.observed: Operator acceptance telemetry and QA evidence are absent across fraud copilot, AML assist, and banker assist use cases.
workforce.matters: Without operator readiness evidence, AI deployment risks low adoption, compliance gaps, and audit findings.
workforce.supports: Workforce readiness assessment and acceptance telemetry design must precede any AI pilot authorization.

apps.meaning: Core banking, digital, fraud, AML, loan, CRM, and risk platforms operate with incomplete integration and lineage evidence.
apps.observed: Cloud lakehouse and customer 360 foundation are target-state only; current-state integration evidence is not confirmed.
apps.matters: Fragmented application estate blocks real-time data flows required for fraud, AML, and customer 360 use cases.
apps.supports: Application integration mapping must precede AI use-case design; target-state platforms cannot be assumed current.

data.meaning: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.
data.observed: Approved answer content, data-quality exceptions, and model-risk approvals lack named owners in current context.
data.matters: Unowned data products and ungoverned AI outputs create audit exposure and slow regulatory response.
data.supports: Ownership assignment is a prerequisite; no AI use case should advance without accountable domain owners confirmed.

infra.meaning: Cloud lakehouse and customer 360 foundation are aspirational; current infrastructure evidence is not yet validated.
infra.observed: Regulatory reporting modernization and customer 360 use cases depend on platforms not yet confirmed as operational.
infra.matters: Assuming target-state infrastructure creates sequencing risk and may delay or invalidate AI deployment timelines.
infra.supports: Infrastructure readiness assessment must precede use-case sequencing; cloud migration status needs evidence.

vendors.meaning: CoreBank, FraudShield, ComplyCase, and others carry unlinked SLA obligations, invoice variances, and exit-right gaps.
vendors.observed: Invoice-to-SOW mapping, rate-card variance, and third-party risk linkage to renewal decisions are not reconciled.
vendors.matters: Unreconciled vendor obligations create financial leakage risk and weaken negotiation leverage at renewal.
vendors.supports: Vendor optimization is a hypothesis; treat negotiation leverage as planning-grade until procurement and legal approve.

budget.meaning: FS Demo operates across lending, cards, payments, fraud, AML/KYC, and wealth under strong regulatory oversight.
budget.observed: Business model is synthetic planning-grade; no real customer, account, or transaction data is claimed or evidenced.
budget.matters: Regulatory exposure across multiple sub-industries amplifies the cost of ungoverned AI or data decisions.
budget.supports: Enterprise profile demands evidence-first sequencing; transformation hypotheses need compliance and risk co-sign.

programs.meaning: Fraud copilot, AML assist, banker assist, regulatory reporting, customer 360, loan automation, and vendor optimization are active hypotheses.
programs.observed: All seven initiatives carry unresolved lineage, control, model-risk, or baseline evidence gaps blocking progression.
programs.matters: Advancing initiatives without evidence resolution risks regulatory findings, model failures, and wasted investment.
programs.supports: Program sequencing must be evidence-driven; no initiative should enter execution without gap closure confirmation.

ai.meaning: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.
ai.observed: Seven use cases span risk, customer experience, operations, and data functions; integration gaps are pervasive.
ai.matters: Siloed functions prevent unified customer view, complicate AI deployment, and fragment control accountability.
ai.supports: Function-level evidence must precede cross-domain AI initiatives; sequencing risk is high without integration proof.

risks.meaning: Regulatory reporting controls, AML reviewer controls, and fair-lending controls lack linkage to certified data products.
risks.observed: Control attestations, audit evidence, and data-quality exceptions are unlinked and owner-unassigned across domains.
risks.matters: Fragmented control evidence creates audit finding risk and delays regulatory response across multiple exam cycles.
risks.supports: Control linkage to data products must be established before any AI or reporting modernization is claimed ready.

rel.meaning: CIO, CTO, CDAO, and CRO signals indicate decision latency, contract friction, and sequencing risk across initiatives.
rel.observed: Interview signals reveal priority clarity gaps and control blockers across technology, data, and risk leadership.
rel.matters: Unresolved stakeholder friction slows evidence collection and delays use-case gating decisions across the enterprise.
rel.supports: Stakeholder alignment on evidence priorities must precede any use-case sequencing or vendor negotiation decisions.

evidence.meaning: No finance-approved baselines, realized savings, or ROI evidence exists for any current AI or modernization initiative.
evidence.observed: False-positive baselines, cycle-time metrics, and handle-time data are absent; value claims remain hypotheses.
evidence.matters: Without spend baselines and value proof, investment prioritization and business case approval are at risk.
evidence.supports: Finance and operations must co-sign baselines before any AI use case advances to investment approval stage.

metrics.meaning: False-positive rates, AML case cycle times, handle times, and defect baselines are absent or not finance-approved.
metrics.observed: Value hypotheses exist for all seven use cases; none are supported by certified operational or financial baselines.
metrics.matters: Without baselines, AI value measurement is impossible and business case approval cannot be credibly supported.
metrics.supports: Baseline definition and finance approval must precede any AI pilot design or vendor value commitment.

industry.meaning: Regulated banking AI adoption patterns consistently require lineage, model-risk, and explainability before production deployment.
industry.observed: FS Demo's gaps mirror industry patterns where governance lag creates supervisory risk and deployment delays.
industry.matters: Industry precedent confirms that ungoverned AI in fraud, AML, and lending attracts regulatory scrutiny and penalties.
industry.supports: Governance-first sequencing is the industry-validated approach; accelerating past controls creates disproportionate risk.

lenses.meaning: Model risk, AML compliance, fair lending, and data governance expert lenses each surface distinct but compounding blockers.
lenses.observed: No single use case is blocked by one gap; each carries multiple expert-domain evidence requirements simultaneously.
lenses.matters: Compounding blockers across expert domains require coordinated evidence collection, not sequential gap closure.
lenses.supports: Multi-domain expert coordination is required; single-threaded evidence collection will not meet deployment timelines.

ms.meaning: RegOps Managed Services is identified as a vendor; scope, SLA linkage, and accountability boundaries are not confirmed.
ms.observed: Managed services dependency for regulatory operations creates risk if scope and controls are not documented.
ms.matters: Ungoverned managed services scope in regulated reporting creates audit exposure and third-party risk gaps.
ms.supports: Managed services scope review must precede regulatory reporting modernization; accountability must be documented.

opev.meaning: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.
opev.observed: Seven use cases span risk, customer experience, operations, and data functions; integration gaps are pervasive.
opev.matters: Siloed functions prevent unified customer view, complicate AI deployment, and fragment control accountability.
opev.supports: Function-level evidence must precede cross-domain AI initiatives; sequencing risk is high without integration proof.

dimensions.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

dimensions.name: Relationships

dimensions.name: Evidence Sources

dimensions.summary: Regulated banking AI adoption patterns consistently require lineage, model-risk, and explainability before production deployment.
